title: Jason Calacanis on virality, learning skills fast, and angel investing for founders
summary: Jason explains why a product customers won't shut up about is the core growth engine, with marketing built on top of it. He also covers resourcefulness (RTFM, reaching 60-70% of any skill in weeks), selling early vs. taking secondary, and how new angels should deploy capital.

principles.text: Virality comes from a product customers can't stop talking about; build everything else around that.
principles.quote: the great products people can't wait to tell their friends about them so it all starts and ends with having a great product

principles.text: Use Net Promoter Score to test for virality; 9-10 scores signal advocates, 7-8 means you'd better have margins or monopolies.
principles.quote: the highest NPS score products are the ones that tend to be like these kind of products that people won't shut up about and they tell their friends about

principles.text: Study your few superfans to find your beachhead; early on, you need learning, not all the answers.
principles.quote: there's one or two people give us a nine or ten and we're studying them to figure out why they love it so much

principles.text: Profitable products can fund marketing; spend a small slice of profit on channels that may not provably work.
principles.quote: if you have a product that makes money and it's profitable and is great you can then spend money marketing it

principles.text: Marketing tactics decay (like infographics), but referral credits that make people feel good giving to friends last.
principles.quote: you have to understand that marketing channels burn out some of them are timeless some of them are have a half-life

principles.text: Basic competence in most skills takes weeks, so skip excuses and learn it yourself before outsourcing.
principles.quote: getting to the base level of skill as an audio engineer in other words understanding 60 or 70 percent of what the best audio engineer knows might take a hundred hours or 50 hours
